This is the written companion to my YouTube episode (React from Scratch #5, in Moroccan Darija): https://youtu.be/UCKbmOi8l4k 1. Start a new project, then clean it up Create a fresh React project and run it locally to confirm everything works. Then delete the demo content you don't need and keep only the base you'll build on. If you haven't met it: Patzer is a self-hosted Chess.com alternative — game review for your real Chess.com/Lichess games, play vs Stockfish or a friend, lessons and an opening trainer, and an AI coach that runs on your own Ollama or vLLM. articles.title: What your money does in a perpetual futures exchange?
articles.excerpt: Imagine you think Bitcoin’s price will rise. You could buy Bitcoin and sell it later. Or you could trade a perpetual future, often called a perp. It is a type of contract whose value follows Bitcoin’s…
articles.body: Imagine you think Bitcoin’s price will rise. You could buy Bitcoin and sell it later. Or you could trade a perpetual future, often called a perp. It is a type of contract whose value follows Bitcoin’s price. You can trade on the price change without owning the Bitcoin itself. A perp has no fixed end date. You can keep your trade open until you close it, as long as you have enough money backing it. That sounds simple, but the exchange has to keep track of your order, your gains or losses, regular funding payments, and the risk that you might lose more than you put up. Let’s follow one example from start to finish. The numbers are simplified, and each exchange has its own rules.

articles.title: Node.js Feature Flags: 3 Evidence Layers for Missing-Key Cohort Rollbacks
articles.excerpt: The bill for troubleshooting missing feature flags in a healthtech tenant experiment includes key lookups, scheduled comparison runs, captured errors, and retained evidence. Safe fallback defaults kee…
articles.body: The bill for troubleshooting missing feature flags in a healthtech tenant experiment includes key lookups, scheduled comparison runs, captured errors, and retained evidence. Safe fallback defaults keep the established workflow active while that investigation proceeds. For a storage design, retained evidence deserves an explicit calculation before anyone proposes keeping every response indefinitely. In an illustrative workload—not a measured deployment—100 tenant cohorts producing one 2 KB summary per day generate 200 KB daily; retaining 30 days requires 6 MB before indexes, replication, and encoding overhead. Keeping 20 KB instead makes that 60 MB. Payload size changes this term tenfold; a different flag service doesn't erase it.

The work will take place at the awardee’s facility. articles.title: How sci‑fi imagines sports in microgravity, and how zero‑g sports might actually work
articles.excerpt: How realistic are the zero-g sports we see in sci-fi? We talk to Les Johnson, former Chief Technologist for NASA, to find out.
articles.body: Sports in space have a long and proud tradition, whether it's Alan Shepard playing golf on the moon or the crew of the ISS hosting their own version of the Summer Olympics . The future looks bright as well, with the foundation of the Space Games Federation , the self-described "first governing and sanctioning body for competitive sports played in zero or micro-gravity," co-founded by a NASA astronaut. Not to be outdone, science fiction has expanded the idea of zero-g and low-gravity sports to their logical extent, imagining everything from Doctor Who's zero-g squash to the advanced, gamified combat simulations of Ender's Game.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 23, 2015: Blue Origin sticks 1st-ever rocket landing from space with its suborbital New Shepard rocket
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 23, 2015, a Blue Origin rocket made a historic landing after launching into suborbital space. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 23, 2015, a Blue Origin rocket made a historic landing. Before this time, all rockets were single-use only — even SpaceX's rockets. Blue Origin changed the concept forever. After launching the New Shepard capsule safely into space, the rocket started heading back to Earth. It flew towards a landing pad, reignited its engine to slow down and touched down softly on the ground . This was the first successful vertical landing from space in history. The Blue Origin milestone meant that rockets could be reused for multiple missions, which saves money and reduces waste. (Image credit: Blue Origin) Why it mattered Today, SpaceX may be the most well-known for landing its Falcon 9 rocket boosters from orbit.

articles.title: Studying Cancer Cells in Microgravity
articles.excerpt: This Nov. 19, 2026, image shows gastric microtumors grown within an Encapsulates biochip. The Encapsulate-1 investigation studies patient-derived tumor samples aboard the International Space Station t…
articles.body: Encapsulate Inc. This Nov. 19, 2026, image shows gastric microtumors grown within an Encapsulates biochip. The Encapsulate-1 investigation studies patient-derived tumor samples aboard the International Space Station to better understand how cancer cells move and interact in microgravity. The results could help researchers develop further testing to predict a patient’s risk of metastasis and support more personalized cancer treatments. Orbiting more than 200 miles (320 km) above Earth, the space station is a powerhouse of cutting-edge science that is unlocking discoveries not possible on Earth. Image credit: Encapsulate Inc.
